Regular expressions

ECMAScript 2026

A regular expression is a pattern for testing or finding text. Use it when you need to match several strings with the same shape, such as an order code.

Open interactive lesson

On this page

  • Check the whole string with test()
  • Find multiple matches and capture groups

Check the whole string with test()

In a literal, slashes surround the pattern. ^ and $ anchor the pattern to the start and end here. [A-Z] matches one uppercase English letter and {2} asks for two. [0-9]{3} asks for three digits.

How to try it Open a browser tab, then open Developer Tools → Console. Type the example or paste it into the Console after reviewing it, then run it. Reload before repeating declarations with the same names.

const orderCode = /^[A-Z]{2}-[0-9]{3}$/;
console.log(orderCode.test("TE-104"));
console.log(orderCode.test("TE-10"));

What to expect The checks print true and false. The second code is missing a digit.

Find multiple matches and capture groups

Use matchAll() with the g flag to visit each match. Parentheses capture a part of a match. The match array contains the full match first, followed by the captured parts. For independent test() calls, omit g and y because they can advance lastIndex on a reused expression.

How to try it Open a browser tab, then open Developer Tools → Console. Type the example or paste it into the Console after reviewing it, then run it. Reload before repeating declarations with the same names.

const line = "pen:3, notebook:2";
for (const match of line.matchAll(/([a-z]+):([0-9]+)/g)) {
  console.log(match[1], Number(match[2]));
}

What to expect The first line prints pen and 3. The second prints notebook and 2.
